---
title: "Isochrones"
format: html
editor: visual
---

An **isochrone** is a line or polygon on a map that connects all points reachable from a specific starting location within a set amount of time

[Inspiration from Kyle Walker](https://walker-data.com/posts/accessibility-surface/)

### Libraries

```{r}
library(mapboxapi)
library(leaflet)
library(mapview)
```

### Create Isochrone

```{r}
isos <- mb_isochrone(
  location = "One Bowerman Dr, Beaverton, OR 97005",
  profile = "driving",
  time = 1:45
)
```

```{r}
mapview(isos, zcol = "time")
```

```{r}
library(sf)
library(fasterize)

isos_proj <- st_transform(isos, 32618)

template <- raster(isos_proj, resolution = 100)

iso_surface <- fasterize(isos_proj, template, field = "time", fun = "min")

iso_surface
pal <- colorNumeric("plasma", isos$time, na.color = "transparent")

nike_map <- leaflet() %>%
  addMapboxTiles(style_id = "light-v9",
                 username = "mapbox",
                 scaling_factor = "0.5x") %>%
  addRasterImage(iso_surface, colors = pal, opacity = 0.5) %>%
  addLegend(values = isos$time, pal = pal,
            title = "Drive-time from<br>Nike HQ")

nike_map
```

```{r}
nike_icon <- makeIcon(
  iconUrl = "https://nike.com/favicon.ico",
  iconWidth = 25,
  iconHeight = 25
)

nike_hq <- mb_geocode("One Bowerman Dr, Beaverton, OR 97005")

nike_map %>%
  addMarkers(lng = nike_hq[1], lat = nike_hq[2], icon = nike_icon)
```

### Lets go further

Question: Can we make an accessibility surfaces map for trauma centers, ER's, hospitals, fire stations etc. Maybe combine all of them into one shiny app. Let's strategise and design...

App Design

fire stations: mb_isocrone works well

ambulance: mb_isocrone works for ambulance to pashunt, but form there

shelters: - Faith

cant go off base travel time in island wide emergency situations

hospitals, trauma centers, etc... - Calvin

senior / other transportation - Drew

police station hostage situation

swim, lifeguard response - DJ

```{r}
# Clear environment and load libraries
rm(list = ls())
library(mapboxapi)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

# Set your Mapbox token globally
my_token <- "pk.eyJ1IjoiY29ubm9yZmx5bm4iLCJhIjoiY2x5cWFtZzk0MGU4MzJqb2F0a2w1bGJkZiJ9.fB81ysj5JOrG16upKvzk4A"

# Step 1: Define the multi-layered dataset with exact addresses
hubs_df <- data.frame(
  name = c(
    "OTS Middle Street (TheHandi-Van)", 
    "Catholic Charities", 
    "Royal Kūpuna Transport", 
    "Pasion Transportation", 
    "Project Dana"
  ),
  address = c(
    "811 Middle St, Honolulu, HI 96819", 
    "1822 Keʻeaumoku St, Honolulu, HI 96822", 
    "2332 Pio Pl, Honolulu, HI 96819", 
    "91-2026 Kamakana St, Ewa Beach, HI 96706", 
    "902 University Ave, Honolulu, HI 96826"
  ),
  service_type = c(
    "Public Paratransit", 
    "Senior Call-Van", 
    "Private NEMT", 
    "Private NEMT", 
    "Volunteer Medical Escort"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Step 2: Geocode addresses individually using rowwise iteration
hubs_sf_list <- hubs_df %>%
  split(1:nrow(.)) %>%
  map(function(row) {
    coords <- mb_geocode(row$address, access_token = my_token)
    st_sf(
      name = row$name,
      address = row$address,
      service_type = row$service_type,
      geometry = st_sfc(st_point(coords), crs = 4326)
    )
  })

hubs_sf <- do.call(rbind, hubs_sf_list)

# Step 3: Call the Mapbox Isochrone API sequentially with 15, 30, 45, and 60-minute time intervals
isochrones_list <- list()

for (i in 1:nrow(hubs_sf)) {
  coords_vector <- as.numeric(st_coordinates(hubs_sf[i, ]))
  
  iso <- mb_isochrone(
    location = coords_vector,
    time = c(15, 30, 45, 60), # Updated intervals
    profile = "driving-traffic", 
    depart_at = "2026-10-12T08:00:00Z", # Configured for a Monday morning rush hour
    access_token = my_token
  )
  
  # Append metadata fields to the output poly
  iso$hub_name <- hubs_sf$name[i]
  iso$service_type <- hubs_sf$service_type[i]
  isochrones_list[[i]] <- iso
}

all_isochrones <- bind_rows(isochrones_list)

# Step 4: Standardize factors for map layering
# Order labels sequentially so they stack nicely in the map legend
all_isochrones <- all_isochrones %>%
  mutate(contour_label = factor(
    paste0(time, " min drive"), 
    levels = c("15 min drive", "30 min drive", "45 min drive", "60 min drive")
  )) %>%
  arrange(desc(time))

# Step 5: Plot separated by Service Type using facet_wrap
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = all_isochrones, aes(fill = contour_label), alpha = 0.4, color = "white", size = 0.1) +
  geom_sf(data = hubs_sf, color = "black", fill = "yellow", size = 3, shape = 21) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(
    direction = -1, # Inverts the scale color order to match travel thresholds smoothly
    name = "Drive Time From Hub"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~service_type) + 
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Oʻahu Specialty Medical Transit Reachability (Expanded)",
    subtitle = "15 to 60-minute isochrones separated by tier (8:00 AM Traffic Grid)",
    caption = "Data modeled using Mapbox Navigation Service API Matrix via mb_isochrone(). Code made with AI (Google Gemini)"
  ) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#fafafa", color = NA)
  )

```
